decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa on 220940-221430s answered 'A panda is being painted...' (correct content), but the agent's final turn emitted plain text 'The streamer painted a **panda** on his face — option 1.' instead of calling submit_answer with a JSON-wrapped answer, causing a pydantic ValidationError ('expected value at line 1 column 1') and attempt failure.
On retry, the agent re-ran the same investigation, pulled episodes rows in the 220954-221494s window, and called submit_answer correctly with the same panda conclusion.

rollouts.failure_point: attempt-1: execution/format failure (agent produced free-text final answer instead of a submit_answer tool call with valid JSON payload), not a retrieval failure — content was already correct.
rollouts.evidence_checked: error.json shows ValidationError on AnswerSubmission from raw string input 'The streamer painted a *... face — **option 1**.'; attempt-2 trace shows the same underlying evidence (episodes window 220954-221494s) reproduced and submitted correctly.

db_evidence.notes: topic_facts:00005977 at 221464s explicitly states 'ishowspeed has panda face paint applied by a woman', and multiple episodes:30sec rows in the 220804-221500s window describe gray/black panda-style eye patches and nose plus panda plushies. The fact is directly retrievable via semantic_search over topic_facts/episodes and via run_sql windowed queries, and clip_qa on the same window independently confirms it visually. This is a well-covered, easy-to-retrieve clue: both direct text semantic search and visual verification converge on the same answer.

root_causes: Not applicable in the failure sense: all 5 rollouts converged on the correct answer (score 5). The clue is redundantly encoded (topic_facts text, episodes captions, and visual frames all say 'panda'), so different retrieval strategies (text-only vs text+clip_qa) all succeeded.

rollout-04 attempt-1 hit a pure execution/format failure — the agent answered correctly in its reasoning but failed to invoke submit_answer with a schema-valid JSON payload, producing a ValidationError that ended the attempt; the harness's retry-to-attempt-2 mechanism then produced a correct, properly formatted submission.
what_worked: semantic_search over topic_facts and episodes with the entity name 'Cang Xiang Shu Ying' plus 'panda/Nezha/Chinese dragon' surfaced the exact scene text directly (topic_facts:00005977, episodes:30sec:007370 etc.) in 3 of 5 rollouts, enough to answer without any visual call.

clip_qa on tightly-scoped windows (e.g. 221100-221450s, 221434-221494s) in the other rollouts gave unambiguous 'a panda' verdicts with evidence_times_s squarely inside total_intervals, so visual verification agreed with text evidence.
run_sql windowed queries around the total_intervals timestamp (220800-221600s) reliably pulled all relevant episode captions describing the panda-themed paint as a cross-check.
transferable_lessons: For entity-recognition questions naming a specific venue (e.g. 'Cang Xiang Shu Ying'), semantic_search over topic_facts/episodes with the venue name plus the answer-option keywords is often sufficient on its own — clip_qa is a helpful but not always necessary confirmation when text evidence is unambiguous.

Always terminate an agent turn by calling submit_answer with the answer as valid JSON payload, never by leaving free text as the final assistant message — a stray natural-language closing sentence without the tool call causes a hard ValidationError and burns an attempt.

When retrieval evidence (text or visual) already converges cleanly on one option, do not second-guess into a wrong hedge; rollout-01's momentary '2? No—' self-correction shows the risk of hesitation phrasing, and only the final resolved answer is judged.
open_questions: Whether the rollout-04 attempt-1 ValidationError (agent ending with plain text instead of a submit_answer call) is a recurring pattern across other questions/rollouts in this run, which would indicate a systemic prompting/tool-use issue rather than an isolated incident.
